finding.message: This callback awaits, so it returns to its caller at the first wait and finishes later — but its result is nothing, so the work in flight has no handle anyone can hold. The caller carries on as though the work were done, several such calls run at once rather than in turn, and a failure after the first wait has nowhere to go: it is raised where nobody catches it, which on some runtimes ends the process. Return the work's handle and have the caller wait for it, or hand the callback to something that waits for what it returns.

Indexing answers "what does this name resolve to", which on an ordinary object includes everything the language put there before the author's own keys — so a key like `constructor` comes back with a value, and it is neither absent nor falsy.
